The file has my changes. But git status says clean. That means the changes are already committed? Or the index somehow... Wait, maybe there's a git hook or the branch already had these changes committed. Let me check `git log -1` and `git show HEAD --stat`.

Actually, "nothing to commit, working tree clean" plus the file containing changes means the changes are in HEAD. Perhaps the task's starting commit already contains the fix? No, initially the file did not contain the guard (I read it before edit at line 20-22 without guard). Hmm.

Wait — maybe a background process committed? Or `git diff` earlier showed nothing because... Let me check git log now.
